title: FluxGuard: A Haptic Flux-Sensing Wristband that Warns and Steers Substation Workers Away from Lethal Induction
content: High-voltage substations are threaded with invisible time-varying magnetic flux. Unlike heat or noise, this field gives the human body no natural warning until induced currents are already stimulating nerve and heart tissue. We propose FluxGuard, a lightweight wristband that watches for hazardous fields with five independent detection methods running in parallel: a three-axis induction-coil sensor (Faraday’s law), a wide-range Hall-effect magnetometer (Lorentz force), a capacitive electric-field probe (displacement current), a tunnelling-magnetoresistive (TMR) bridge (spin-dependent tunnelling), and an ultrasonic corona listener (acoustic emission of partial discharge). The five channels are fused by first-detect-wins (1-out-of-5 OR) trigger logic: whichever method crosses its threshold first fires the alarm. The band estimates the direction of decreasing exposure using a short-baseline gradiometer, hardened by three independent bearing estimators with confidence-gated voting—a wrong arrow is never shown; on disagreement the guidance degrades gracefully to a memoryless “warmer/colder” closed loop—and warns the wearer through a directional haptic (vibration) cue—long before contactlevel currents become dangerous. Redundant sensing across five distinct physical principles, continuous self-test, an analog comparator fast path that bypasses the firmware, and a latching fail-safe alarm make the architecture robust to any single sensor, filter, or software fault. Because a startled wearer may panic, collapse, or forget which way is “away”, a cognition-free guidance suite—withdrawal-reflex lateral haptics, a zero-memory “warmer/colder” closed loop, a world-locked escape arrow, spoken escort commands, and automatic man-down SOS—keeps steering (or summoning rescue for) the wearer even when judgement fails. We present the physical principles, full block and circuit diagrams, a build guide, and a feasibility-to-integration analysis of embedding the same function in an ordinary smartphone augmented with an external high-flux sensor pod. A safety panel quantifies exactly how much current the human body tolerates before perception, loss of muscular control, and cardiac fibrillation.
